 Ford, Toyota, BMW, GM and Dodge Vehicles Recalled
 Free Press Publisher 
 November 2, 2026 
 Lifestyle and Travel News , Notices 
 Ford: Tailgate Cable May Fail — Recall 26V689 
 Ford Motor Company is recalling certain trucks because a tailgate cable may fail. Affected models include:
 2026–2027 Ford F-150
 2026 Ford F-250 SD
 2026 Ford F-350 SD
 2026 Ford F-450 SD
 Toyota: Seat Back May Unlatch During Crash — Recall 26V690 
 Toyota Motor Engineering & Manufacturing is recalling certain vehicles because a seat back may unlatch during a crash. The affected model is:
 2022–2026 Toyota Sienna Hybrid
 BMW: Engine Starter Battery Connection May Loosen — Recall 26V695 
 BMW of North America is recalling certain vehicles because the engine starter’s positive battery connection may loosen. Affected models include:
 2018–2020 BMW 530e iPerformance
 2018–2020 BMW 530e xDrive iPerformance
 2018 BMW 740Le xDrive iPerformance
 General Motors: Insufficient Front-Seat Welds — Recall 26V696 
 General Motors is recalling certain vehicles because of insufficient welds on the front seats. Affected models include:
 2026 Chevrolet Traverse
 2026 GMC Acadia
 Dodge: Tail Lights May Fail — Recall 26V701 
 Chrysler, also known as FCA US, is recalling certain vehicles because the tail lights may fail. The recall references Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 108. The affected model is:
 2026 Dodge Durango
 Owners can check whether their specific vehicle is affected by entering their license plate number or vehicle identification number in NHTSA’s recall lookup tool . If a vehicle has an unrepaired recall, owners should contact their local dealership to schedule a free repair.

 Email: info@fcfreepress.com Who We Are
 The Franklin County Free Press, established by Vicky Taylor in 2019, emerged as a beacon of local journalism for the residents of Franklin County. Under Vicky's leadership, it quickly became an essential source of news, particularly at a time when major newspaper publications were increasingly overlooking local coverage. 
On January 1, 2022, the torch was passed to Nathan Neil and his firm, Neil Publishing, LLC. Neil, a local entrepreneur with multiple thriving businesses in Chambersburg, shares Vicky's fervent commitment to both the community and the world of local journalism. 
Rooted in the heart of Franklin County and powered by its residents, the Franklin County Free Press continues to bridge the gap, ensuring that the local stories, events, and issues that matter most to the community remain in the spotlight.
